newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria levies tax to undercut Moslem rebels.
newsitem.headline: Algeria levies tax to undercut Moslem rebels.

text.p: The Algerian government imposed on Thursday special taxes on house owners and traders in Algiers in an effort to solve the capital's housing and unemployment crises which feeds support for Moslem rebels.

Algerian state-run radio said each house owner would have to pay 300 dinars ($5.3) a year and each shopowner 1,200 dinars ($21.4) and that the money raised would be channelled to housing projects for the poor.
More than three million people live in the city, many in overcrowded appartments housing 10 or 12 people.
The tax was announced one day after the government adopted a special plan to fight unemployment, chronic accommodation problems and other social woes plaguing the capital.
Officials say Algiers is still the main recruiting ground for guerrilla factions, many of whose leaders come from Algiers.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
